Title: Diagnosis

Details: The issue report concerns the behavior of the 'node()' test implementation in the DOMNodePointer class, specifically at line 120 in DOMNodePointer.java. The report states that the code currently only treats ELEMENT_NODE and DOCUMENT_NODE as nodes that match the 'node()' test.

Looking at the implementation of the method `DOMNodePointer.testNode(Node node, NodeTest test)`:

- At line 146-148 (inside the NODE_TYPE_NODE case), the return statement is:

  ```
  return nodeType == Node.ELEMENT_NODE || nodeType == Node.DOCUMENT_NODE;
  ```

- According to the XML and XPath data model, the 'node()' test should match any node type, not just elements and documents. This means all node types such as text nodes, comments, processing instructions, etc. should be matched by 'node()'.

- The current implementation, therefore, is restrictive and inconsistent with the expected behavior of the 'node()' node test in XPath.

The failing test case involves an XPath expression selecting following nodes, which may include other node types than elements and documents. Because the method incorrectly excludes these nodes during matching, the test fails.

Hence, the root cause is that the 'node()' test only matches ELEMENT_NODE and DOCUMENT_NODE in `DOMNodePointer.testNode` method, whereas it should match all node types by simply returning true in that case (i.e., when the node test type is NODE_TYPE_NODE).

This diagnosis matches the bug report comment exactly and explains why the test involving following nodes does not pass as expected.

Summary:
- The bug is in the line `return nodeType == Node.ELEMENT_NODE || nodeType == Node.DOCUMENT_NODE;` inside `DOMNodePointer.testNode`.
- The fix is to change this line to `return true;` to correctly implement the 'node()' test per the XPath specification.

This explains the failing test on node axis navigation with 'node()' tests.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
